items.title: Pass the helped command's positional args to the help function
items.description: A help function installed with Command.SetHelpFunc(func(c *cobra.Command, args []string)) is not given the positional arguments of the command being helped. When help is requested with the -h/--help flag (e.g. `root sub arg1 arg2 -h`) the function receives the raw argument vector that Execute was given, including the subcommand name, every flag and the help flag itself (["sub" "arg1" "arg2" "-h"]). The same raw vector is passed when a command without a Run is invoked (the reporter's `sub` has no Run), with or without -h. When help is requested through the built-in `help` command (e.g. `root help sub arg1 arg2`) the function receives an empty slice. In every case the help function is invoked for the correct command, but with the wrong args, so a help function that wants to vary its output on what the user typed cannot. Expected: in all paths the help function receives exactly the positional (non-flag) arguments that follow the command path, as a Run function would (flags and flag values stripped in `--flag value`, `--flag=value` and bool forms; everything after `--` kept as positional), e.g. ["arg1" "arg2"]; and requesting help must not leave state behind that changes a later Execute on the same root. Issue: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2154 (kind/bug, area/cobra-command, OPEN). Behaviour lives in the root `cobra` package, command.go: the flag.ErrHelp branch of (*Command).ExecuteC (reached both when --help is set and when the command is not runnable) and the Run of the default help command built in (*Command).InitDefaultHelpCmd. Scope note: the no-help-flag non-runnable case is one line of the same ErrHelp branch and is not literally named in the issue; it is asserted so the fix lands in that branch rather than only in the --help check inside execute().
acceptance_criteria: Given root with a runnable subcommand `sub` (declaring an int flag --count and a bool flag --verbose) and a help function set via root.SetHelpFunc, executing `sub arg1 arg2 -h` invokes the help function exactly once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly ["arg1" "arg2"], and sub's Run does not execute.

Given the same tree, the help function receives exactly the positionals with every flag and flag value stripped: `sub -h arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub --count 3 arg1 --help` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --count=3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --verbose arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; and `--` ends flag parsing so `sub -h arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"].

Given `sub` without a Run (the issue's program), `sub arg1 arg2 -h` invokes the help function once for "sub" with ["arg1" "arg2"], and `sub arg1` (no help flag; help is shown because sub is not runnable) invokes it once for "sub" with ["arg1"].

Given the same tree, `help sub arg1 arg2` invokes the help function once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly ["arg1" "arg2"] (not an empty slice); with a child `nested` added to sub, `help sub nested arg1` invokes it once for "nested" with ["arg1"].
After `help sub arg1` on a root, executing `sub` on the same root runs sub's Run exactly once and does not invoke the help function again (the help command leaves no flag or argument state behind).
Execute returns a nil error in all of the above cases, and the help function is invoked for the helped command (not the root or the help command).

All existing tests in the root `cobra` package and in `./doc` still pass (`go test -count=1 ./...`), `go vet ./` and `gofmt -l .` are clean, and the public API (SetHelpFunc, HelpFunc, Help signatures; Help() still passes []string{}) is unchanged.
structural_facts: reproduction: root := &cobra.Command{Use: "root"}; sub := &cobra.Command{Use: "sub", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}; root.AddCommand(sub); root.SetHelpFunc(func(c *cobra.Command, args []string) { fmt.Printf("%s %q\n", c.Name(), args) }); root.SetArgs([]string{"sub", "arg1", "arg2", "-h"}); root.Execute() prints `sub ["sub" "arg1" "arg2" "-h"]`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "arg1", "arg2"}); root.Execute() prints `sub []`; with sub having no Run, root.SetArgs([]string{"sub", "arg1"}); root.Execute() prints `sub ["sub" "arg1"]`.

expected_behaviour: the help function receives the positional arguments of the helped command with the command path and all flags (and flag values, in `--flag value`, `--flag=value` and bool forms) removed and `--` honoured, in both the flag.ErrHelp branch of (*Command).ExecuteC (reached when --help is set and when the command is not runnable; the command's flags have already been parsed there, so cmd.Flags().Args() holds the positionals) and the `help <path to cmd> <args...>` path (the default help command's Run in (*Command).InitDefaultHelpCmd, where (*Command).Find(args) returns the command and its remaining args as its second result); the help command must not mutate root's args or the helped command's flags; the helped command passed as the first parameter stays the same, and Help() keeps its signature and its []string{} argument.

exact_value: `sub arg1 arg2 -h` -> args ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub -h arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub --count 3 arg1 --help` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --count=3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --verbose arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -h arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"]; non-runnable sub: `sub arg1 arg2 -h` -> ["arg1" "arg2"], `sub arg1` -> ["arg1"]; `help sub arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `help sub nested arg1` -> c.Name()=="nested", ["arg1"]; after `help sub arg1` a following `sub` runs sub's Run once with the help function called 1 time in total; c.Name()=="sub" and exactly one help-function call in every other case.

items.title: Built-in help and completion commands fail when a persistent flag is marked required
items.description: When an application marks a persistent flag on its root command as required (root.PersistentFlags().Bool("required", ...); root.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("required")), the sub-commands cobra generates itself become unusable unless the user also passes that flag: `prog help`, `prog help <child>`, and `prog completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` (with or without --no-descriptions) all return the error `required flag(s) "required" not set` instead of printing the help text / completion script. Command.ValidateRequiredFlags() (command.go) runs for every command, including the help command built in Command.InitDefaultHelpCmd() and the completion command (and its bash/zsh/fish/powershell sub-commands) built in Command.InitDefaultCompletionCmd() (completions.go), and the required persistent flag is inherited by all of them. These cobra-built commands never consume the user's flags, so the required-flag validation must not apply to them. Scope: the exemption applies to the command OBJECTS cobra constructs in InitDefaultHelpCmd / InitDefaultCompletionCmd, identified by identity (e.g. an unexported marker on those literals, or a hook attached to those literals), NOT by command name: a user-defined sub-command named `completion` (which replaces cobra's default one), `bash`, `powershell`, or a help command supplied via SetHelpCommand is user code and must keep required-flag enforcement. The fix must also keep (a) flag parsing on the built-in commands (`help -h`, `completion bash -h`, `completion bash --no-descriptions` must still work), (b) required-flag enforcement on the user's own commands, and (c) the root command's PersistentPreRun/PersistentPreRunE hook running for the built-in commands (a fix that adds a PersistentPreRun to the built-in commands without chaining to the root's hook would shadow it and break existing CLIs). Keep the change minimal and free of incidental refactors (no renaming of string literals to constants etc.): a marker-based or hook-based fix is 10-35 non-test lines. Issue: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1918 (kind/bug, area/cobra-command; maintainer confirmed it as a bug).
acceptance_criteria: With a root command whose persistent flag `--required` is marked required via MarkPersistentFlagRequired, `root help` and `root help child` return a nil error and print the target command's help (root.Long / child.Long, usage line) without the text `required flag(s) "required" not set`.

With the same root, `root completion bash`, `root completion zsh`, `root completion fish` and `root completion powershell` return a nil error and print the completion script (e.g. bash output starts with `# bash completion V2 for root`); `root completion bash --no-descriptions` still parses its own flag and emits a script requesting `__completeNoDesc`.

`root help -h` and `root completion bash -h` return a nil error and print the help of the built-in sub-command itself: `root help -h` output contains "Help provides help for any command in the application." and "Usage:\n  root help [command] [flags]"; `root completion bash -h` output contains "Usage:\n  root completion bash" and "--no-descriptions" (flag parsing on the built-in commands is not disabled).

Required-flag enforcement is unchanged for user commands: `root child` (and `root` itself) still fail with exactly the error `required flag(s) "required" not set`, and `root child --required` succeeds.

The exemption is by identity of the cobra-built command objects, not by name: with a user-defined sub-command `completion` added via root.AddCommand (cobra then does not create its own), a user-defined sub-command `bash`, a user-defined sub-command `powershell`, or a user help command installed via root.SetHelpCommand, running `root completion` / `root bash` / `root powershell` / `root help` without the flag still fails with exactly `required flag(s) "required" not set`, and each succeeds with `--required`.

The root command's PersistentPreRun is still invoked exactly once (with the executed command: named "help" for `help` and `help child`, "bash" for `completion bash`) when `help`, `help child` or `completion bash` runs, and an error returned by the root's PersistentPreRunE is returned unwrapped (same error value) from Execute for `root help`; `go test -count=1 ./...` passes and `gofmt -l .` is empty.
structural_facts: reproduction: root := &cobra.Command{Use: "root", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}; root.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{Use: "child", Run: ...}); root.PersistentFlags().Bool("required", false, ""); root.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("required"); root.SetArgs([]string{"help"}); err := root.Execute() -> err.Error() == `required flag(s) "required" not set`; the same happens for args {"help", "child"}, {"completion", "bash"}, {"completion", "zsh"}, {"completion", "fish"}, {"completion", "powershell"} and {"completion", "bash", "--no-descriptions"}. The error comes from (*Command).ValidateRequiredFlags in command.go, which (*Command).execute calls for every command, including the ones created by (*Command).InitDefaultHelpCmd (command.go) and (*Command).InitDefaultCompletionCmd (completions.go).

expected_behaviour: the help command and the completion command (and its bash/zsh/fish/powershell sub-commands) that cobra constructs itself must not validate the user's required flags: Execute() returns nil and writes the help text / completion script to the command's OutOrStdout. The exemption is tied to the command objects built in InitDefaultHelpCmd / InitDefaultCompletionCmd (identity), not to the names help/completion/bash/zsh/fish/powershell: user-defined commands with those names (root.AddCommand(&Command{Use: "completion"}), Use: "bash", Use: "powershell", or root.SetHelpCommand(&Command{Use: "help"})) keep failing with the exact error when the flag is missing. The behaviour must hold while (1) flag parsing on the built-in commands stays enabled (`help -h`, `completion bash -h`, `completion bash --no-descriptions` keep working), (2) user commands keep failing with the exact error `required flag(s) "required" not set` when the flag is missing, and (3) the root's PersistentPreRun / PersistentPreRunE still runs once for the built-in commands and a PersistentPreRunE error is returned unwrapped from Execute (do not add a PersistentPreRun hook to the built-in commands that shadows the root's hook).

exact_value: `root help` output contains "Long description of root" and "Usage:
  root [flags]
  root [command]"; `root help child` output contains "Long description of child" and "Usage:
  root child [flags]"; `root completion bash` output contains "# bash completion V2 for root" and not "__completeNoDesc"; `root completion bash --no-descriptions` output contains `requestComp="${words[0]} __completeNoDesc ${args[*]}"`; zsh output contains "#compdef root", fish "# fish completion for root", powershell "# powershell completion for root"; `root help -h` output contains "Help provides help for any command in the application." and "Usage:
  root help [command] [flags]"; `root completion bash -h` output contains "Usage:
  root completion bash" and "--no-descriptions"; `root child`, `root` (no args), and user-defined `root completion` / `root bash` / `root powershell` / SetHelpCommand'd `root help` return exactly `required flag(s) "required" not set` (and nil with `--required`); the root PersistentPreRun receives the executed command, named "help" for `help` / `help child` and "bash" for `completion bash`, exactly once; a root PersistentPreRunE returning err makes `root help` return that same err value.
